title: Flagged at the Border
script: Narrator: [tense] Something about my landing card must have caught the officer's eye, because I was pulled from the queue and led to a side room without explanation.
Narrator: [anxious] Nobody had done anything wrong, as far as I could tell, yet the mere act of being singled out made me feel instantly, irrationally guilty.
Narrator: [reflective] I sat there rehearsing my own itinerary in my head, as though I might somehow forget why I'd come, or where I was even staying.
Narrator: [observant] Across the room, an elderly man was being questioned far more thoroughly than I was, his passport passed between three different officials.
Narrator: [thoughtful] It occurred to me that the randomness of these checks is rarely as random as the system likes to claim.
Narrator: [honest] I'd never once been stopped like this on my other passport, the one issued by a wealthier, more trusted country.
Narrator: [wry] Privilege, I realised, isn't only about money; it's also about which document you happen to be holding at a border.
Narrator: [calm] When the officer finally called my name, she asked a handful of routine questions, then apologised for the delay almost as an afterthought.
Narrator: [measured] I wanted to be angry, and part of me was, but another part recognised that her apology cost her nothing while my hour had cost me plenty.
Narrator: [reflective] Walking out, I passed the elderly man again, still waiting, his shoulders slightly stooped under the fluorescent lights.
Narrator: [warm] I caught his eye and offered a small, useless smile, the only gesture available to a stranger in that particular room.
Narrator: [thoughtful] Later, on the train into the city, I found myself wondering how many trips are quietly reshaped by moments like that one.
Narrator: [honest] Not ruined, exactly, but tilted, coloured by a reminder that borders were never designed to treat every traveller equally.
Narrator: [determined] I don't have a tidy conclusion, only a resolve to notice, next time, whose passport lets them walk straight through.
Narrator: [reflective] Travel teaches you as much about the systems you move through as it does about the places you're heading to.
Narrator: [with a small smile] I still travel constantly, and I still love it, but I no longer pretend the process is neutral for everyone.

quiz.question: Why was the narrator pulled from the queue at the border?
options: The reason was never explained to her
quiz.explanation: She was led to a side room without explanation, and never learns exactly why she was singled out.
